title: mail-server: Email filter evaluator (AND/OR/NOT, all Email/query conditions); memory Email/query uses it
description:
Design: docs/design/emailpush.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: E3. Crates: jmap-mail-server. Size: M.

Spec: draft-ietf-jmap-emailpush-05 §4 (MUST support AND/OR/NOT; with mail every Email/query FilterCondition, else at least hasKeyword, notKeyword, from, to, cc, bcc, subject, header, minSize, maxSize), RFC 8621 §4.4.1, RFC 8620 §5.5. Design: docs/design/emailpush.md §5.4, §10 "mail-server filter".

Add crate-private crate-jmap-mail-server/src/filter.rs, built under cfg(feature = "memory") for now (the emailpush skeleton bead widens it to any(memory, emailpush)): email_matches(&DeliveredEmail, &EmailFilter) -> Result<bool, EmailPushError> (or a local error type that the skeleton bead maps), conditions_used(&EmailFilter) -> BTreeSet<EmailCondition>, a #[non_exhaustive] pub enum EmailCondition covering every RFC 8621 §4.4.1 condition plus the six metadata-05 conditions, and EMAIL_PUSH_REQUIRED_CONDITIONS: [EmailCondition; 10] in §4 order. Text conditions use a case-insensitive substring test built on jmap-metadata-server unicode_casemap_prepare. An unknown Operator/Filter variant is an error, not true. Thread conditions take thread keywords and return MissingThreadKeywords when absent, never a silent pass. Switch the memory Email/query from the private email_matches_condition (memory/mod.rs), which today ignores maxSize, from, to, cc, bcc, subject, header, text, body and the thread conditions, to this evaluator. The memory backend supplies the thread keywords. This is a wire behaviour change for memory only: note it in CHANGELOG.
Acceptance: a positive and a negative test for each of the 10 required conditions; AND, OR and NOT, including NOT over several conditions (none match); the §5 OR filter matches by mailbox and by $notify; a thread condition without thread keywords => error; memory Email/query regression tests for from, subject and maxSize. The non-mail support-set check (which conditions an account allows) is in the validation bead (JMAP-r44n.5).
